passages.provision_quote: (3) For taxable years beginning after December 31, 2016, and before January 1, 2023, three and twenty-three hundredths percent (3.23%). (4) For taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022, and before January 1, 2025, three and fifteen hundredths percent (3.15%).
passages.note: Enrolled act text printing the cut to the individual adjusted gross income tax rate, plus repeal of the utility receipts tax; no deleted-fence text is quoted.
Senate vote on Conference Committee Report #1 passed 50-0, so under V4 this vote cannot carry the chair on its own.
passages.actor_quote: Bray Ford Jon Mishler Walker K

rows.reasoning: Mishler was the Senate sponsor of HB 1002 (2022), whose operative sections cut the individual adjusted gross income tax rate from "three and twenty-three hundredths percent (3.23%)" to "three and fifteen hundredths percent (3.15%)" with a conditional phase-down to 2.9%, and repeal an entire tax ("SECTION 3. IC 6-2.3 IS REPEALED" — the utility receipts tax). That is "Cut taxes broadly, including the main rates most people pay": it reaches the rate every resident pays, so it is more than "targeted adjustments — closing loopholes or granting narrow relief". The rung above it is excluded by the act's own text, which makes each further cut contingent on general fund revenue growth of at least two percent and on the pension stabilization fund being sufficient, and which shrinks no government function — not "as far as possible and shrink what government does".
